title: Could humans have 33 senses?
titleChinese: 人类可能拥有 33 种感官吗？
paragraphs: Many of us grew up learning that humans have five senses: sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch - an idea dating back to the Ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle. But what if this list is incomplete? A sense is anything that can give your body information about the outside world, and some of these don't neatly fit into the traditional five. Modern scientists estimate there may be up to 33 different senses.

One sense that doesn't fit into one of the five boxes is proprioception. This is the sense of where your body parts are in space. Thanks to this sense, you can touch your nose with your eyes closed and walk around in the dark - you know where your legs are without looking. Then there's interoception which helps you sense things inside your body, like hunger and an increased heart rate. And don't take your sense of balance for granted. Balance relies on fluid in your inner ear to help you stay upright - this is what's called vestibular perception.

And the traditional five senses might not be as simple as they seem. Touch, the sense we associate with our hands and tactile sensations, also encompasses the sensation of pain, temperature and itch. To perceive the flavours in food and drink, you need a combination of taste, smell and touch to get the full experience - it's not all about the taste buds on your tongue! It is actually smell that contributes most of what we perceive as taste, so when a person suffers olfactory loss, they often can't enjoy food as much, according to a 2022 study published in Foods by Fjaeldstad and Smith.

Until recently, philosophers and scientists have studied each of the traditional five senses in isolation, but researchers at the University of London's Centre for the Study of the Senses have more of a multisensory approach - the senses are all working together to create an overall picture. In their 'Rethinking the Senses' project, they found that our perception of salt, sweet and sour flavours is reduced when there is white noise, but our perception of umami is not. This means that sound can enhance flavour, and that umami-rich foods like tomato juice might taste better on a plane.

So, perhaps humans are far more sensory creatures than Aristotle ever imagined. From balance and body awareness to the way sound can change flavour, our senses are constantly working together in ways we rarely notice.
chineseParagraphs: 我们中的许多人从小就知道人类有五种感官：视觉、听觉、味觉、嗅觉和触觉——这一观念可以追溯到古希腊哲学家亚里士多德。但如果这个列表不完整呢？感官是任何能让你的身体获取外部世界信息的东西，而其中一些并不能恰当地被归入传统的五种之中。现代科学家估计可能有多达33种不同的感官。
一种无法归入五类的感官是本体感觉。这是感知你身体各部分在空间中所处方位的感官。多亏了这种感觉，你可以闭着眼睛触摸到鼻子，在黑暗中行走——你不用看就知道你的腿在哪里。还有内感受，它能帮助你感知身体内部的情况，比如饥饿和心率加快。也不要认为你的平衡感是理所当然的。平衡依赖于内耳中的液体来帮助你保持直立——这就是所谓的前庭觉。

传统的五种感官可能并不像它们看起来那么简单。触觉，这种我们将手和触觉感受联系在一起的感官，也包括疼痛、温度和瘙痒的感觉。要感知食物和饮料的味道，你需要味觉、嗅觉和触觉的结合才能获得完整体验——这不仅仅关乎你舌头上的味蕾！实际上，我们感知为“味道”的大部分其实是嗅觉贡献的，所以当一个人失去嗅觉时，他们通常无法像以前那样享受食物，根据Fjaeldstad和Smith 2022年发表在《Foods》上的一项研究。
直到最近，哲学家和科学家们还一直孤立地研究传统的五种感官，但伦敦大学感官研究中心的 researchers 则采用了更多多感官的方法——各种感官共同协作，创造出整体画面。在他们的“重新思考感官”项目中，他们发现当存在白噪音时，我们对咸、甜、酸味的感知会减弱，但对鲜味的感知则不会。这意味着声音可以增强风味，而像番茄汁这样富含鲜味的食物在飞机上可能味道更好。
所以，也许人类远比亚里士多德所想象的更具感官性。从平衡和身体意识到声音改变风味的方式，我们的感官一直在以我们很少注意到的方式协同工作。

vocabulary.entry: date back to /ˌdeɪt ˈbæk tu/ phr. 追溯到，始于（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The tradition of drinking tea dates back to ancient China.
vocabulary.translation: 饮茶的传统可以追溯到古代中国。

vocabulary.entry: philosopher /fɪˈlɒsəfə(r)/ n. 哲学家（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The philosopher wrote extensively about ethics and morality.
vocabulary.translation: 这位哲学家撰写了大量关于伦理和道德的著作。

vocabulary.entry: incomplete /ˌɪnkəmˈpliːt/ adj. 不完整的，未完成的
vocabulary.example: The report was rejected because it was incomplete.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告因不完整而被退回。

vocabulary.entry: neatly /ˈniːtli/ adv. 整齐地，恰当地
vocabulary.example: The problem doesn't fit neatly into any category.
vocabulary.translation: 这个问题不能恰当地归入任何类别。

vocabulary.entry: estimate /ˈestɪmeɪt/ v. 估计，估算
vocabulary.example: We estimate the journey will take two hours.
vocabulary.translation: 我们估计这段路程需要两小时。

vocabulary.definition: 本体感觉（生理学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: proprioception /ˌprəʊpriəˈsepʃn/ n. 本体感觉（生理学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Proprioception allows you to know where your limbs are without looking.
vocabulary.translation: 本体感觉让你不用看也知道你的四肢在何处。

vocabulary.definition: 内感受（生理学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: interoception /ˌɪntərəʊˈsepʃn/ n. 内感受（生理学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Interoception helps you sense hunger and thirst.
vocabulary.translation: 内感受帮助你感知饥饿和口渴。

vocabulary.entry: heart rate /ˈhɑːt reɪt/ n. 心率（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can help lower your resting heart rate.
vocabulary.translation: 定期锻炼有助于降低静息心率。

vocabulary.entry: fluid /ˈfluːɪd/ n. 液体，流体（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The doctor told him to drink plenty of fluids.
vocabulary.translation: 医生告诉他多喝流质。

vocabulary.entry: inner ear /ˌɪnər ˈɪə(r)/ n. 内耳（解剖学术语）
vocabulary.example: The inner ear is responsible for hearing and balance.
vocabulary.translation: 内耳负责听觉和平衡。

vocabulary.definition: 前庭的（解剖学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: vestibular /veˈstɪbjʊlə(r)/ adj. 前庭的（解剖学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Vestibular disorders can cause dizziness.
vocabulary.translation: 前庭疾病会导致头晕。

vocabulary.entry: tactile /ˈtæktaɪl/ adj. 触觉的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Tactile sensations are processed by the skin.
vocabulary.translation: 触觉感受由皮肤处理。

vocabulary.entry: encompass /ɪnˈkʌmpəs/ v. 包含，涵盖（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The curriculum encompasses a wide range of subjects.
vocabulary.translation: 课程涵盖广泛的学科。

vocabulary.entry: sensation /senˈseɪʃn/ n. 感觉，知觉（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The pain produced a burning sensation in his chest.
vocabulary.translation: 疼痛在他的胸部产生了一种灼烧感。

vocabulary.entry: itch /ɪtʃ/ n. 痒，瘙痒
vocabulary.example: He scratched the itch on his arm.
vocabulary.translation: 他抓了抓手臂上的痒处。

vocabulary.entry: perceive /pəˈsiːv/ v. 感知，察觉（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He is perceived as a very wise man.
vocabulary.translation: 他被认为是一个非常智慧的人。

vocabulary.entry: taste bud /ˈteɪst bʌd/ n. 味蕾（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Spicy food can stimulate your taste buds.
vocabulary.translation: 辛辣食物能刺激你的味蕾。

vocabulary.definition: 嗅觉的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: olfactory /ɒlˈfæktəri/ adj. 嗅觉的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Olfactory receptors are in the nose.
vocabulary.translation: 嗅觉感受器位于鼻子中。

vocabulary.definition: 孤立地，单独地（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: in isolation /ɪn ˌaɪsəˈleɪʃn/ phr. 孤立地，单独地（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: He worked on the project in isolation for months.
vocabulary.translation: 他独自一人在这个项目上工作了数月。

vocabulary.definition: 多感官的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: multisensory /ˌmʌltiˈsensəri/ adj. 多感官的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The museum offers a multisensory experience.
vocabulary.translation: 博物馆提供多感官体验。

vocabulary.entry: white noise /ˌwaɪt ˈnɔɪz/ n. 白噪音（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: White noise can help some people sleep.
vocabulary.translation: 白噪音可以帮助一些人入睡。

vocabulary.entry: umami /uːˈmɑːmi/ n. 鲜味
vocabulary.example: Mushrooms and soy sauce have a strong umami flavour.
vocabulary.translation: 蘑菇和酱油有浓郁的鲜味。

vocabulary.entry: enhance /ɪnˈhɑːns/ v. 增强，提高（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The new software enhances the user experience.
vocabulary.translation: 新软件增强了用户体验。

vocabulary.entry: sensory /ˈsensəri/ adj. 感官的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Sensory information is processed by the brain.
vocabulary.translation: 感官信息由大脑处理。

vocabulary.entry: constantly /ˈkɒnstəntli/ adv. 持续不断地，经常地
vocabulary.example: He is constantly being reminded to improve his behaviour.
vocabulary.translation: 他不断被提醒要改善自己的行为。
